newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea bans Hanbo chairman from leaving country.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea bans Hanbo chairman from leaving country.

text.p: South Korea's Justice Ministry said on Saturday it had banned seven executives of troubled Hanbo Group from leaving the country.
The ministry said the ban was imposed against founder Chung Tae-soo, chairman Chung Bo-keun and five other executives bacause of suspected financial irregularities.
"We believe there were illegal borrowing by Hanbo executives," ministry spokesman Chung Yoon-sup told Reuters. "The departure ban became effective from January 24."
Hanbo Steel Corp, the flagship company of the group, defaulted on payments of more than five billion won worth of promissory notes.
Government officials said excessive investment in building a steel mill in the southern city of Tangjin was a main reason for the problem.
Hanbo Steel said it was saddled with a debt totalling 5.7 trillion won ($6.7 billion).
The finance ministry said loans from financial institutions amounted to 4.95 trillion won, against its net worth of 224.3 billion won.
